title: structured(output): add CFG/regex constrained decoding backend + tokenizer edgecase fixes
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: add extensible constrained-decoding backends to the structured-output API surface to support CFG/grammar rules and regex-based constraints while fixing tokenizer edge cases that caused constraint violations mid-stream. This PR introduces a backend abstraction (ConstrainedBackend) and two implementations: CFG backend (earley-based validator + partial-acceptor) and Regex backend (incremental DFA engine). It also bumps the OpenAI-compat layer to ensure constrained streaming semantics and updates the streaming encoder to better handle subtoken boundaries so constraints are evaluated on stable token prefixes.

What this changes: - core: new constrained_decoding/ backend interface and registry - runtime: integrate chosen backend into the streaming pipeline; add fallback policy when a backend signals dead-end (graceful rollback to unconstrained or alternative model variant) - openai-compat: expose constraint config in the streaming/protocol layer and preserve backpressure semantics - tokenizer: fix edgecases where byte-level splits created invalid intermediate tokens for regex/grammar checks; adds canonicalization step before evaluation - tests: unit + integration tests for CFG and regex backends, fuzzing harness for tokenization constraints - docs/examples: example grammar and regex constraint snippets added to redwood-docs/examples - metrics: new metrics for constraint-matching latency, constraint-failure-rate, and fallback-counts

Compatibility & migration notes: This is backward-compatible for users who don't enable constrained decoding. For OpenAI-compat users, constrained options are opt-in via the new `constraints` field. There is a small behavior change for streaming when constraints are enabled: the runtime may emit short-lived 'partial-constraint' tokens during early prefix checks; clients should rely on final structured outputs or the provided rejections/fallback signals.

Testing & perf: - Local benchmarks on a production-like workload (mix of short chat turns + structured responses) show ~5-12% additional CPU overhead in the streaming path when using regex backend, and ~8-18% for CFG depending on grammar complexity. - Added integration smoke tests to CI and a dedicated perf canary job to track constraint overhead over time.

Rollout plan: - Feature flagged behind `constrained_decoding_v1` - Start with opt-in beta for internal teams and a small group of customers - Monitor new metrics + perf canary for 2 weeks before wider opt-in

Checklist: - [x] Backend interface + CFG and Regex implementations - [x] Tokenizer fixes and canonicalization - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] OpenAI-compat layer update - [x] Docs and examples - [x] Metrics and canary integration

Related: ENG-4123 (design doc), ENG-4201 (perf tuning), SUP-879 (customer request for structured grammar support).

review_comments: Marcus Patel (review): Can we avoid a full Earley re-run on every prefix? Looks expensive for long sequences.

Ava Chen (reply): We added a partial-acceptor optimized for prefix checks; the implementation caches state per stream and prunes unreachable states. Added benchmarks in the PR description and a microbenchmark file.
Sofia Ramirez (review): Tokenizer fixes LGTM but please add a comment about why canonicalization is safe for multilingual scripts.
Ava Chen (reply): Added explanatory comment and a unit test covering Japanese and Arabic edgecases (combining marks).
Diego Alvarez (review): CI flaked on integration-tests; saw timeout in first run. Recommend extending test timeout and rerunning canary.
Ava Chen (reply): Increased timeout and split the longest integration scenario into a separate job; CI passed on rerun.
ci_checks: perf-canary: scheduled (baseline run added to perf pipeline)
release_notes: Add v1 constrained decoding backends (CFG & regex) behind feature flag. Tokenizer canonicalization to avoid false negative constraint matches. Opt-in via `constraints` field in OpenAI-compat and Redwood API. Observe constraint metrics and fallback behavior during rollout.
